name: html-nested-style-rule-attribute-selector-projection
description: Nested style rules project like their flat equivalents. Selector analysis only read top-level rules, so a nested rule gated by source attributes (`.menu{&[data-mode=v]{&[layout=one] .item{...}}}`) was emitted verbatim: lowering dropped the attributes and moved the class it selected, and the vertical-menu padding and item separators stopped applying. Nesting is now desugared at input, so the ungated and the attribute-gated item rules both reach the emitted link, and the gated one still wins by its higher specificity.

source_reference.notes: Product-neutral fixture: site builders ship stylesheets compiled with native CSS nesting.
